answers.label: Benefits and challenges of consequential methods
answers.text:
As a leading battery energy storage developer in the United States, esVolta acknowledges that a consequential accounting method is necessary to accurately characterize the system-level impact of energy storage.
We strongly support the consequential method as a means of incentivizing and rewarding energy storage systems for their role in decarbonizing the electricity grid. In addition, this method is the only way to measure real-world carbon impacts, which are not measured under attributional accounting methodologies. Therefore, the consequential method must be incorporated within the GHG Protocol alongside attributional methods.

answers.label: Appropriateness of the TWG subgroup formula
Why the formula is or is not appropriate
answers.text:
The proposed formula as currently drafted only accounts for avoided emissions and does not account for induced emissions. At esVolta, we evaluate the avoided emissions of our battery energy storage projects by taking the difference of the induced emissions caused by charging the batteries and the avoided emissions by discharging the batteries. Were we to measure our avoided emissions without subtracting our induced emissions, our inventory would be inaccurate and hugely overstate the avoided emissions of our facilities.
• Induced Emissions: MWh (charging) * Marginal Emission Rate

• Avoided Emissions: MWh (discharging) * Marginal Emission Rate

• Total Avoided Emissions: Avoided Emissions – Induced Emissions

audit_basis: A US battery-storage developer and operator; an asset owner rather than a retail energy supplier.
